title: Persistent Meta-Shelf: compact contextual shelf for workspace routing and cost-aware lanes
creator: Lina Patel
description: Problem: Workspace switching and route discovery in the Redwood Console is fragmented — users lose context when switching models, routes, or rollout variants. Cost and rollout signals are buried in per-page panels and not visible during quick navigation. Goal: Design a compact, persistent "meta-shelf" — a minimal horizontal strip that sits above content and provides contextual workspace routing, active route breadcrumbs, quick rollout toggle, and a lightweight cost summary. It should be visible on narrow viewports and collapse into an affordance when space is constrained. This ticket covers UX exploration, prototype, usability review, and handoff artifacts for engineering implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates meta-shelf states: expanded, compact, collapsed with hover affordance
User tests show >=80% of participants can switch workspace and change active rollout variant within 3 interactions
Cost summary displays 3 metrics (estimated token cost, recent median latency, caching hit-rate) and updates within 500ms of route switch in the mock
Design spec includes responsive behaviors, a11y color contrast tokens, keyboard focus order, and ARIA labels
Handoff includes annotated component tokens and interaction states for engineering to implement a stable API surface
decision_points: Show/hide cost metrics by role: default on for admins, collapsed for contributors — decision: default collapsed for contributors, can pin for role via settings
Rollout toggle mechanism: in-shelf dropdown vs inline radio — decision: inline micro-toggle with confirmation for traffic changes
Placement: top-of-page shelf vs left-rail extension — decision: top-of-page shelf to minimize left-rail changes and preserve vertical space
tradeoffs: Shelf increases visual density at the top of the page; we mitigate with compact tokens and progressive disclosure
Embedding cost telemetry in the navigation reduces cognitive separation but may nudge users toward cost-driven decisions — include explicit 'why this number' tooltip
Implementing live cost and latency metrics requires new tracing hooks in runtime; dependency on ENG-22487 increases schedule risk
comments: 2025-02-17 Lina Patel: Initial kickoff, sketched three variants (tabs, chips, shelf). Shared Figma link and asked for engineering feasibility check.

2025-02-20 Marco Chen: Reviewed variants. Engineering flagged live cost updates as high effort due to tracing API gaps (linked ENG-22487). Recommended a progressive enhancement approach: mocked values initially, stream later.
2025-02-27 PM Elena Ruiz: PM review — emphasize rollout controls and safety (must include soft-confirm). Added PM acceptance criteria and requested integration with Rollouts dashboard.

2025-03-03 Research: 5 usability sessions with internal power users. Observations: participants preferred inline micro-toggle and a single-line breadcrumb showing pinned model, route, and rollout. Two users asked for quick 'open console route' keyboard shortcut.
2025-03-08 Design critique: Move cost metrics to the right side of shelf and use micro-sparkline for token trend. Agreed to add an optional pinned state to keep shelf visible.

2025-03-12 Marco Chen: Prototype v2 delivered (figma). Engineering notes added to comments with API surface suggestions and estimated backend work: 6 sprint points for streaming metrics once ENG work finishes. Flagging dependency ENG-22510 for rollout toggle backend support.
prototype_notes: Prototype v1: chip-based shelf with dropdown route list; static cost numbers
Prototype v2: inline micro-toggle for rollouts, compact sparkline for cost, keyboard-accessible nav focus ring
Animation: shelf expands with 160ms ease, collapse 120ms; prefer snappy collapse on scroll
Responsive: on widths <960px shelf collapses into a single 'shelf pill' that expands on click
usability_findings: Mean completion time for switching route in prototype v2: 2.1s
Error rate: 0.9% where users accidentally changed rollout variant — resolved via soft-confirm and undo snackbar
Participants rated 'visibility of cost' 4.2/5 for usefulness but 3.1/5 for clarity; need better tooltip copy
